item.body:
Closes #657
Claim: ext/francoisgn-readme

**Problem.** README of `dev-swift` had stale milestone figures (dated 2026-11-06, M4 "1 of 23", M5 "0 of 30"), stale phase counts (2026-11-01), no M5 content beyond a paragraph, an outdated "How it is built", and a contributing section missing steps (labels, session-id format, `REVIEW WANTED`, ledger, `/release`, PR limit). Support was at the bottom. The roadmap SVG showed M1–M4 only, with figures of 2026-10-29.

**Cause.** The milestone table is hand-written: nothing in `tooling/roadmap/` generates README (only the board comments), so no generator to fix. The SVG is generated from `docs/assets/source/roadmap/elements.json`.

**Changed (docs only, no macOS jobs).**
- `README.md`:
  - `> [!NOTE]` support block under the title: Leetchi link + existing Leetchi badge; Apple Developer account $99 per year, image-hosting API $170 per year (operator precision), shared effort. `## Support` is now a short pointer.
  - "Where we are": no-public-build note (M1 lots done; LOT-161 #251 left, the M1 exit check; #344 and #322 closed on 2026-11-01); phase table without stale counts; milestone table with M1–M5 in one format plus a progress column.
  - "Big topics planned in M5": 7 grouped bullets linking the issues.
  - "How it is built" and "Contributing": rewritten as links to AGENTS.md, ORCHESTRATION, REVIEW-ROUNDS, CONTRIBUTING, EXTERNAL-AGENTS, MAC-SESSIONS. No rules copied; no CONTRIBUTING/EXTERNAL-AGENTS gap needed filling. The ledger rule links tooling/docs/README.md#the-ledger-rule and AGENTS.md §8 (#620/#621).
- Roadmap SVG (operator: change if needed): `elements.json` gets an M5 box and arrow from M4, the figures of the 2026-11-08 boards, and M4's text without the "iOS 27 experience" moved to M5; `roadmap-milestones.svg` and `.excalidraw` regenerated with the documented `export.js` (rendered and checked by eye); alt text in README and `docs/ROADMAP.md` mentions M5; the source README says M2–M5.

**Sources of numbers** (snapshot 2026-11-08): board body of #324 (M2 28/28 100 %, M3 38/43 88 %, M4 4/26 15 %, M5 0/29 0 %) and #166 (M1 40/40 100 %). M5 lots and scope notes: #324 M5 section and ezzz's comments of 2026-11-07/08 on #233, #234, #418, #421, #422, #242, #243, #244.

**Not done / to flag.**
- Stale board items reported on #324, and on #166 (#344, #322 still listed as todo).

**Tests.** `npx markdownlint-cli2@0.18.1` on the changed `.md` files: 0 errors; `python3 scripts/check-lot-deps.py` OK. CodeRabbit: 2 rounds, 4 minor findings fixed, threads resolved. Opus review at 3e42882: 7 findings, fixed in 7fd1b48.

Review wanted: Opus (author model: Sonnet 5.5).

- The README table is not generated: `tooling/roadmap/` has no README writer. The steward refreshes it by hand from the board render (#544, #585, #650). The PR's "no generator to fix" is right.
- Every anchor resolves on `dev-swift`: ORCHESTRATION `#claims` and `#child-sessions-cloud`; EXTERNAL-AGENTS `#4-…`, `#5-…` and `#the-open-pr-limit` (under §10); CONTRIBUTING `#1-…` and `#2-merge-criteria`; AGENTS `#6`, `#7` and `#8`. MAC-SESSIONS and REVIEW-ROUNDS exist.
- M5 list, spot-checked against ezzz's PO comments of 2026-11-07:
  - #233 (iPad / unfolded Duo, behind a setting): faithful.
  - #418 (discreet marker, no banner): faithful.
  - #244 → #627 (counter-proposal): faithful.
  - #625 for the quick-reply bar (tray out): faithful.
- No ledger path touched (rule #620). No secrets. The only login is the public `francoisgn`. The support note's tone is plain and factual. "Mostly links, no copied rules" holds.

**Findings**

1. **Major — README.md:17-18 (support note); also the PR body ("existing Buy Me a Coffee badge").** The branch is based on `b38de53` (2026-11-06). That base predates #553 (operator, 2026-11-07), which *replaced* the Buy Me a Coffee badge with the Leetchi pot. The note re-adds the BMC badge, and the issue asks to "move the Leetchi badge up". On merge this silently undoes an operator decision.
   *Fix:* merge `dev-swift` and put the existing Leetchi badge (from #553) in the note. Drop the BMC badge unless the operator asks for both.

2. **Major — the PR conflicts with `dev-swift`; CI has not run.** `mergeable_state: dirty`: README.md conflicts with #553, #544, #585 and #650. On head `3e42882`, only gitleaks/Secret scan and CodeRabbit ran. None of the 9 required checks ran (Docs consistency, markdown links, …), so the merge criteria cannot hold.
   *Fix:* merge `dev-swift` (current `53170bb`) and resolve README.md, keeping this PR's table and the Leetchi badge. A hand-resolved conflict needs a new round (REVIEW-ROUNDS: give the `--remerge-diff` result). Then get the required checks green.

3. **Major — README.md:83 ("Where we are" note).** It says that before the first TestFlight build, two Mac hand checks are left: #344 and #322. Both were **closed on 2026-11-01** (`Done in #381 (merged as 4e6a3ff)`). The #166 body (snapshot 2026-11-07) still lists them as todo, so the board is stale and the README copies a false fact. A visitor reads that blockers remain that are already done.
   *Fix:* say only LOT-161 (#251) is left. Report the stale #344/#322 rows on #166, as the PR did for #324.

4. **Medium — README.md:169 and :218 (ledger rule).** #621 is merged, so the rule is current. But both lines link the issue #620, not the rule's owner, and step 5 leaves out what a newcomer must actually do:
   - write a `### Ledger` section with fenced `changelog` / `gap-new` / `gap-edit` blocks;
   - add the label `ledger` (no entry: no section, no label).

   The issue asks for "write the ledger" to be reachable by a link to the rule. #620 is the discussion; the owner is [AGENTS.md §8](AGENTS.md#8-git-and-pr-workflow) and [`tooling/docs/README.md`](tooling/docs/README.md#the-ledger-rule). Without them, a contributor following the README fails `Docs consistency` (label and section must agree).
   *Fix:* on both lines, name the `### Ledger` section and the `ledger` label, and link `tooling/docs/README.md#the-ledger-rule` (keep #620 as history if wanted). Also drop the PR-body caveat "AGENTS.md §8 may still describe `changelog-legacy.d` fragments": on `dev-swift` it describes the ledger.

5. **Low — README.md:216 ("the `status: claimed` label follows").** Per AGENTS.md §5/§7 and ORCHESTRATION "Still manual until the workflows are on `master`", nothing syncs `/claim` today. The orchestrator or the maintainer sets `status: claimed` by hand. The README implies automation that does not run.
   *Fix:* "the orchestrator or the maintainer then sets `status: claimed` (by hand until the claim workflow runs from `master`)", or simply link ORCHESTRATION#claims for it.

6. **Low — README.md:163 ("sub-orchestrators and child sessions each take one issue, with one claim per session").** ORCHESTRATION#claims says the orchestrator claims for the child sessions it launches and passes the same id to each child. So a child does not make its own claim. "Sub-orchestrators" appear in no linked document.
   *Fix:* "the orchestrator claims each issue it hands out and passes that id to the child session working it".

7. **Low — README.md:167 ("docs-only and engine-only PRs skip the macOS jobs they do not need").** Per CONTRIBUTING §2, the app build is skipped only when a PR touches none of `App/`, `Packages/` or `ci.yml`. An engine-only PR (`Packages/`) runs both macOS jobs. CodeQL Swift is off the PR gate unless labelled `codeql` (#477).
   *Fix:* "docs-only PRs skip the macOS jobs; CodeQL Swift runs only on PRs labelled `codeql`".

Not blocking: the M5 list leaves out #416 (nothing left beyond parity) and #423 (first-use notice). That is acceptable for a "big topics" list.

Verdict: **REQUEST CHANGES**. Findings 1–3 must be fixed (operator decision reverted, conflict / no CI, false status). 4 is required by the issue's participation-guide criterion. 5–7 are wording.
